data.author: Alex MacDonald
data.summary:
Death toll from Israeli strikes in Gaza rises to six
Israeli strikes killed at least six Palestinians in two separate attacks in the Gaza Strip on Wednesday, the territory's health officials said.
Medics said an Israeli air strike on a vehicle killed at least four people and wounded 14 others in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood in Gaza City, while an earlier air strike on an apartment elsewhere in the city killed a woman.
Later on Wednesday, an Israeli air strike outside a mosque in Khan Younis killed one person and wounded others, medics said, taking the day's death toll to at least six.
The Israeli military did not immediately comment on any of the reported strikes.
Reporting by Reuters.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Muqtada al-Sadr says US should compensate Iraqis as last American forces leave
Influential Shia cleric Muqtada al-Sadr has said the US should compensate Iraqis for the damage inflicted on the country, as the last American troops pull out of Iraq.
In a statement on Wednesday, which is the deadline for American forces to end their 12-year presence in the country, Sadr hailed the "independence of Iraq" and praised those who fought against the US.
"We demand compensation from the American army for all the damages that occurred as a result of its occupation of Iraqi lands," he said.
"Everyone should file legal complaints regarding this."
The US first occupied Iraq in 2003 following the overthrow of Saddam Hussein, before pulling out its forces in 2011.

Israeli settlers raid West Bank village, Ottoman-era historic site
Israeli settlers have been raiding the village of Awarta, south of Nablus, and the area surrounding al-Uzair shrine for more than 12 hours, Wafa news reported.
Local sources told Wafa that dozens of settlers raided the village in the occupied West Bank under protection from Israeli forces, and performed Jewish rituals at Islamic shrines in the village, attacking Palestinians who attempt to approach the site.
Meanwhile, Wafa also reported that Israeli settlers raided the Ottoman-era tunnel known as “Al-Kharq,” east of Bal'a town, east of Tulkarm, on Wednesday.
According to witnesses, they performed Jewish prayers inside and raised Israeli flags.
The tunnel dates back to the late 19th century and has been included on Palestine’s tourism map as one of the country’s notable archaeological sites in need of attention, rehabilitation, and restoration.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iraq celebrates as last US troops withdraw from country
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Iraq celebrates as last US troops withdraw from country
The US removed its last troops from Iraq on Wednesday, 23 years after Washington invaded the country to topple former Iraqi President Saddam Hussein from power, in an intervention that cost over $1 trillion and led to hundreds of thousands of deaths over the last two decades.
"Today, the United States and our Coalition partners formally concluded Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq, consistent with the September 2024 US-Iraq joint statement and US national interests," the Pentagon said in a statement.
The US first occupied Iraq in 2003, following the overthrow of Hussein, before pulling out its forces in 2011. They returned at the request of the Iraqi government in 2014 to tackle the spread of the Islamic State (IS) militant group, which had seized around a third of the country.
The US began withdrawing troops from Iraq in 2025, with soldiers relocating from Ain al-Asad base in Anbar Province and the Victory Base Complex, located within the Baghdad International Airport, to Iraq’s semi-autonomous Kurdish region.
Iraqi Kurdistan was granted some semi-autonomy in 2005. For example, it has its own prime minister, president, and a separate security force, the Peshmerga.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UN condemns Israel's treatment of Palestinian prisoners
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
UN condemns Israel's treatment of Palestinian prisoners
Deputy head of UN Human Rights in Palestine Neil Tobin said on Wednesday that, as of September 2026, more than 9,000 Palestinians are being held in Israeli prisons.
Speaking at the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council, Tobin said a third of Palestinians in Israeli prisons are being held under administrative detention, while more than 1,000 from Gaza are detained as "unlawful combatants", also a form of administrative detention.
"The routine use of administrative detention – on security grounds without criminal charge or trial - continues to expose Palestinian detainees to prolonged arbitrary deprivation of liberty, torture and other ill-treatment and enforced disappearance," Tobin was quoted as saying in a post on X.
Tobin said the situation has deteriorated since October 2023, citing 92 Palestinian deaths in Israeli custody, including 17-year-old Walid al-Basha, who died in an Israeli prison in March 2025 with severe signs of starvation.
“Unless and until each death is the subject of an investigation that meets international standards and disproves allegations of wrongdoing, Israel remains responsible for every single death in custody,” Tobin added.
He called for “regular and unhindered access by independent monitoring bodies with confidential access” to all Palestinian detainees, and for the release of all Palestinians held arbitrarily in Israeli prisons.
